title: Franklin D. Roosevelt & Frances Perkins (1882–1945 / 1880–1965) — Triangle Fire, Steel Braces, Social Security, and the Arsenal of Democracy

teenKit.tldr: When America was collapsing in 1933, a paralyzed president and a fearless chemist teamed up to rewrite the rules of modern society. Frances Perkins used absolute political leverage to force a radical blueprint for workers' rights before she even took the job.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Almost every safety net you rely on today—from weekends and minimum wage to Social Security—exists because two master strategists refused to accept a broken system as permanent.
keyTakeaways: Your maximum leverage in any negotiation happens right before you say yes; once you accept unconditionally, your bargaining power drops to zero.
Franklin D. Roosevelt used brilliant physical stagecraft to hide his paralysis, projecting unflappable strength through radio 'Fireside Chats' when the nation was in a panic.
Frances Perkins's non-negotiable seven-point ultimatum transformed the Department of Labor from a dead-end political payoff into the engine of the American middle class.

vocab.meaning: Carefully managing physical presentation and media to project a specific image or emotional state to the public.
The strategic advantage or bargaining power you hold that forces the other side to meet your demands.

quiz.question: When did Frances Perkins present her seven-point policy ultimatum to FDR?
options: During a live radio broadcast to the American public
Right after she was sworn into office as Secretary of Labor
Before she accepted the job, while she still held maximum leverage
At a congressional hearing investigating the Triangle Shirtwaist Fire
quiz.explanation: Perkins handed over her demands before saying yes, knowing an appointee loses all bargaining power the moment they unconditionally accept a position.

quiz.question: How did FDR communicate directly and calmly with the American public during the banking crisis?
options: Through intimate radio broadcasts known as 'Fireside Chats'
By publishing a daily newspaper column distributed nationwide
Through weekly newsreels played aggressively in movie theaters
By touring every state in a heavily armored train
quiz.explanation: FDR used the radio to speak directly into American living rooms with calm reassurance during moments of national panic.

quiz.question: What traditional view of the U.S. Secretary of Labor position did Frances Perkins instantly shatter?
options: That it required a background in high-level military strategy
That it was just a decorative patronage payoff for male trade union bosses
That it had the power to override state governors and shut down banks
That it was exclusively reserved for former U.S. Presidents
quiz.explanation: Instead of acting as a rubber stamp for union barons, Perkins turned the office into an aggressive policy engine for working people.
